answer: For terrace irrigation decisions, an agent graph can assign each vertex voting weight equal to its locked stake. The kernel snapshots unique deposit IDs before a ballot, keeps the coins locked until it closes, and rejects reuse across keys. Splitting 1,000 coins among 100 aliases still yields only 1,000 votes. If the frozen total is 10,000, a majority requires more than 5,000 locked coins. This needs correct escrow and snapshot accounting; rich attackers or borrowers with sufficient capital can still dominate.
